newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 3.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday :
* Stocks ended mixed on Monday as investors sold blue-chip shares to buy stocks of smaller companies in Wall Street. The Dow Jones industrial average fell 41.64 points to 7,289.40.

* Indonesia May consumer price index is seen rising 0.18-0.20 percent month/month vs 0.56 percent in April. The official inflation figure will be announced on Wednesday after the regular monthly cabinet meeting.

* Indonesia has deployed at least 3,000 troops on Madura island off eastern Java after riots sparked by anger over the ruling Golkar's sweep of general election results, police said on Monday. The re-vote in Sampang is scheduled for Wednesday.

* On Monday, Jakarta stocks ended higher but profit-taking near the close eased strong gains posted earlier in the day, brokers said. The index rose 3.70 points, or 0.53 percent, to 699.73 points after touching a high of 701.75 points.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,429.50/30.50 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.00/30.00.
* Conglomerate Bimantara Citra on reports that it cut its Cakra and Nenggala sedan cars prices after cutting cost production by using 20 percent local content.
* Blue chip automaker Astra International on market speculations of a possible stock split, brokers said.
* Timber firm Barito Pacific after it announced a higher first quarter net profit of 31.0 billion rupiah, compared to 25.8 billion rupiah in the year-ago period.

* Industrial estate developer PT Surya Semesta after it announced first quarter net profit of 28.28 billion rupiah, against net loss of 10.03 billion rupiah in the same period last year. Also on intense market talk that a conglomerate would buy a stake in the firm.
* Small property firm Mas Murni Indonesia on its announcement of slightly higher first quarter net profit of 4.01 billion rupiah, against 3.79 billion rupiah in the same period in 1996.
* Property firm Lippo Land on reports that the firm will buy a 15 percent stake in its sister company Lippo Karawaci from the bourse.
* The country's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur following encouraging net profit in the first quarter of 1997, and on Monday's announcement that it plans to raise its paid-up capital.
* Toll road operator Citra Marga said on Monday it will hold a shareholders' meeting on June 17 to discuss its proposed rights issue.
* Retailer Multipolar and supermarket Hero on renewed market speculation that Multipolar would buy a stake in Hero in the second half of this year.
